source_documents.title: Exciton Coupling and Conformational Changes Impacting the Excited State Properties of Metal Organic Frameworks

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission maximum shifts considerably from 2.87 eV in ethanol to 2.63 eV in the MOF
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in solution and Zn-ADB SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Spectra from earlier experimental work reproduced/discussed in this computational study.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source reports a small absorption red shift and a larger emission red shift when ADB is incorporated into the MOF.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The experimental spectra originate in cited reference 51; they are not new measurements generated by this computational paper.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Both orbitals are largely localized on the central anthracene unit.
reference_evidence_units.subject: isolated ADB
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PBE0 calculations of the lowest singlet transition, Fig. 2 and Table 1.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The HOMO, LUMO and transition density are predominantly localized on the anthracene core, with weak solvent dependence.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Localized orbital character does not support assigning generic donor-acceptor ICT solely from terminal acid groups.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the optically weakly allowed Sb state comes to lie lowest in energy
reference_evidence_units.subject: anthracene model dimer
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Slip scan for simplified anthracene dimers modeled on the framework geometry.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slip changes the ordering of bright and dark states; at the framework-like slip the lowest state is weakly allowed.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This simplified model is not the full ADB framework calculation; target-specific calculations below test the same explanation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the angle between the phenylene and anthracene planes is reduced from 81
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Periodic PBE reference structure and PBE0-D3 cluster optimization.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Neighboring linkers induce conformational changes and greater conjugation relative to an isolated node-linker unit.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Fixed node positions and finite-cluster approximations constrain the geometry; no source SMILES adjudication is implied.

reference_evidence_units.quote: there are two competing effects regarding the change in the absorption spectrum
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Full node-linker dimers/tetramers versus isolated units.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Conformational planarization red-shifts absorption while H-type coupling blue-shifts the strong transition; their combination explains the small net red shift.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: A red absorption shift alone would misidentify this system as purely J-type.

reference_evidence_units.quote: what counts for the emission characteristics according to Kasha’s rule
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Absorption is dominated by strongly allowed higher states whereas emission comes from weakly allowed S1. The source explicitly follows Kasha's rule.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absorption into a higher state is not anti-Kasha emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: massive, excitation-induced conformational changes, as one would expect in classical excimers, do not play a role.
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB in Zn-SURMOF-2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of ground- and excited-state geometry and coupling.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The newer analysis explains the red emission through slipped H-aggregate excitonic coupling rather than a classical strongly relaxed excimer.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The family still includes aggregate excitons; rejection of a classical excimer must not delete all aggregate-coupling support.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the particularly low oscillator strength of 0.06
reference_evidence_units.subject: ADB framework tetramer
reference_evidence_units.conditions: S1 emission calculation at relaxed geometry; comparison to previously reported overall lifetime.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The small calculated emission oscillator strength motivates a long radiative lifetime and a possible time-dependent spectral contribution from different local environments.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Overall lifetime around 4 ns is not the radiative lifetime. Sample inhomogeneity is a proposed explanation, not directly imaged here.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The framework fixes relative linker arrangements and alters conformations, jointly determining the spectra.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Slipped H-aggregate coupling is central; the source distinguishes it from conventional excimer relaxation.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Computed bright/dark state ordering and oscillator strengths distinguish absorption-dominant states from S1 emission. This overlaps with exciton coupling.
